name: GitHub PAT Leaked in CI Build Log
description: A debug `set -x` left in a GitHub Actions workflow echoes a long-lived org-scoped PAT into a public build log. Within 90 seconds an automated scraper finds it. The token is used to clone 12 private repos and add a deploy key to one of them.
reasoning: GitHub Enterprise + the Actions runner pool are the affected services. The simulation focuses on the post-leak misuse: a single token is now the most active git client on the planet for ~10 minutes.

narrative.text: Steady baseline; CI pipelines green; ~40 actions runs in flight.
Public build run echoes 'Authorization: token ghp_***' to logs (set -x in the workflow).
GitHub secret-scanning alert fires — but the token is also already being used elsewhere.
Token used from 23.224.x.x: rapid sequence of repo clones (12 private repos in 4 minutes).
Attacker adds a deploy key to repo 'infra-prod' — would survive PAT revocation.
Audit team revokes PAT, removes the deploy key, force-pushes audit cleanup.
Repo-by-repo review of last 24h commits; nothing rewritten. Notification to affected owners.
All steady. Org-wide rule: no long-lived PATs; only fine-grained or App tokens.
